profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting for a six-week pilot study in a psychiatric neuroimaging lab that wants to brief its institute's steering committee on whether deep neural networks are worth pursuing for structural MRI-based depression research. The team plans to reuse a multi-site adolescent depression MRI collection and the lab's existing 3D CNN codebase to produce an initial result set that highlights both promise and pitfalls, especially around heterogeneity, confounding, and generalization. The agenda is to agree on the cohort preparation, what counts as external validation, who handles the clinical and technical pieces, and what needs to be ready by the end of the month. The expected outcome is a shared-looking plan with task ownership and a timeline for a pilot analysis package.

members.name: Dr. Lena Vogt
members.expertise: Clinical psychiatry, neuroimaging biomarkers, translational ML study design
members.background: Leads a hospital-affiliated research group studying MRI markers of adolescent mood disorders and often positions methods work for grants and clinical collaborations rather than immediate publication.
members.private_state: She wants a credible, clinically interpretable pilot for the steering committee that shows the lab can say something balanced about deep learning without getting stuck in months of engineering or over-cleaning the sample into something clinically unrealistic.
hidden_assumptions: "External validation" means testing on a genuinely independent hospital cohort that was not part of model development, not just a held-out subset from the same consortium.
"Clean cohort" means removing obvious MRI QC failures and mislabeled scan dates while retaining common comorbidities and medication variation so the sample still reflects real psychiatric practice.

"Pilot-ready results" means a stable analysis with one convincing figure and defensible caveats that is sufficient for an internal steering-committee update, even if the pipeline is not yet publication-complete.

When the team says they will use the existing adolescent depression mirror, the clinically usable subset is assumed to be immediately available and not something that needs a new round of narrowing before modeling.

members.name: Arjun Patel
members.expertise: Deep learning for medical imaging, multi-site robustness, reproducible experiment pipelines
members.background: Joined from a computational imaging lab where models were expected to be paper-ready from the first serious run, with strong emphasis on dataset curation, repeatability, and leave-site-out evaluation.
members.private_state: He wants this pilot to become the backbone of a workshop submission and is trying to avoid wasting compute on a noisy cohort or on results that will have to be rerun because the analysis was not rigorous enough.
hidden_assumptions: "External validation" can reasonably mean leave-one-site-out testing within a multi-site consortium if the held-out site was never seen during training.
"Clean cohort" means aggressively reducing label noise and confounds by excluding unstable medication status, ambiguous diagnoses, and frequent psychiatric comorbidities before training.
"Pilot-ready results" means a rerunnable experiment package with fixed seeds, confidence intervals, baseline comparisons, and enough documentation that it can be extended directly into a paper.
If a cohort is described as ready in the lab mirror, that still implies he should apply the usual downstream exclusion logic before calling it analysis-ready.

misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means evaluation on an entirely independent hospital cohort outside the development sample.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means leave-one-site-out evaluation within the same multi-site consortium, where one scanner site is excluded from training.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML and neuroimaging meetings, both usages can sound professionally legitimate and both are framed as testing generalization, so the phrase creates false consensus without either person feeling a need to unpack it.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the clean cohort
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means scans passing image QC with diagnosis matched to scan timing, while retaining typical psychiatric heterogeneity such as anxiety comorbidity and medication use.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a narrower subset that additionally excludes common comorbidities, recent medication changes, and borderline or unstable cases to reduce label noise.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both participants see their own exclusion boundary as the obvious meaning of doing careful science, and neither boundary sounds controversial when referred to only as making the cohort "clean."

misalignment_points.surface_form: "pilot-ready results by the end of the month"
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means one stable result figure and a concise narrative with caveats for an internal steering-committee discussion.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a reproducible experiment package with enough checks and documentation that it can serve as the starting point for a paper submission.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like ordinary planning shorthand, and both interpretations are compatible with being diligent; the difference lies in the evidentiary threshold rather than the visible task label.

By pilot-ready results by the end of the month, I mean one stable, interpretable figure and a sober narrative about what deep learning can and cannot say in this setting. It does not need to be publication-complete; it needs to be solid enough for an internal decision point.
